title: Sharat Saxena, 76, Shares Standing MRI Photos Ahead of Lumbar Spine Surgery
excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor, last seen in Son of Sardaar 2, posted pictures from Mumbai's Bombay Hospital and told fans he hopes to walk properly and work again.
body:
• Veteran Hindi cinema actor Sharat Saxena, 76, posted four photographs from a standing MRI session at Mumbai's Bombay Hospital on September 9.
  • The scan was carried out ahead of scheduled lumbar spine surgery; Saxena captioned the post "Standing mri before lumbar spine surgery at Bombay Hospital."
  • Responding to the flood of fan messages, the actor said he hopes to "walk properly" again and return to work.
  • The engineering graduate turned actor has appeared in more than 250 films across five decades in Hindi, Telugu, Malayalam and Tamil cinema.

Veteran Bollywood actor Sharat Saxena has shared a personal health update ahead of major surgery, posting photographs of himself undergoing a standing MRI at Mumbai's Bombay Hospital and revealing that he is scheduled for lumbar spine surgery.

The 76-year-old actor, who was recently seen in Ajay Devgn-starrer Son of Sardaar 2, published four pictures from the MRI room on social media on September 9. The photographs show Saxena strapped upright to the scanner, with the strain of the procedure visible on his face. In his caption, he wrote simply: "Standing mri before lumbar spine surgery at Bombay Hospital."

The post drew an immediate outpouring of concern and good wishes from fans and well-wishers in the comments. Saxena personally replied to many of the messages, thanking supporters and striking a hopeful note about his recovery.

"Thank you all for the good wishes. I hope I will be able to walk properly and work again. Thank you all."

— Sharat Saxena, replying to fans on social media

Five Decades in the Spotlight

Saxena's path to cinema was unconventional. After completing an engineering degree, he chose acting over a conventional career — a decision his father initially resisted before the family eventually accepted it. Over the decades that followed, he built one of the most recognisable character-actor careers in Hindi cinema, reportedly appearing in more than 250 films across Hindi, Telugu, Malayalam and Tamil cinema.

He is best known to generations of moviegoers as Daga, one of the henchmen of the iconic villain Mogambo in the 1987 blockbuster Mr. India. His filmography includes memorable turns across genres: he played Kareena Kapoor Khan's father in Salman Khan's Bajrangi Bhaijaan, the comic gangster Tota Seth in the Hera Pheri franchise, and roles in Tridev, Ghayal, Khiladi, Soldier and Baghban — moving fluidly between villainous, comic and paternal characters.

A Familiar Face for the Diaspora

For Indian audiences abroad, Saxena is one of those faces that instantly signals a certain era of Hindi cinema. His films — from Mr. India to Baghban — remain staples of family movie nights in NRI households, and his recent appearance in Son of Sardaar 2 showed he was still actively working. His message to fans — that he hopes to "work again" — underlines that he views the surgery as a step toward resuming the career he still pursues in his mid-70s.

What's Next

Saxena has not disclosed the date of the surgery or the expected recovery timeline. Standing MRIs, which image the spine under the body's own weight, are commonly used ahead of spinal procedures to assess problems that may not be visible in conventional lying-down scans. Fans continue to post wishes for a speedy recovery, and the industry will be watching for his return to sets once he has healed.
